payload.name: Category-instance search diversification
payload.description: When a question asks for instances of a category (e.g., activities, hobbies, interests, foods) and initial retrieval yields no clear instance, run additional searches with concrete candidate terms and synonyms, not repeated identical queries.
content: When a question asks to enumerate instances of a category (activities, hobbies, interests, foods, etc.), derive candidate instance terms from the question, from any retrieved memories, and from common subcategories; run separate searches for each candidate term combined with the subject.

If a search for category instances returns only peripherally related memories (e.g., a company, a place) and no concrete instance, reformulate the query with synonyms and specific examples of the category before concluding; do not rerun the same query with only depth or top_k changed.

solves: The agent failed to retrieve a memory naming a concrete outdoor activity because it repeated the same category-label query with only depth changed. Category-enumeration questions (activities, hobbies, interests, features, items) often have evidence stored under specific instance terms rather than the category label, so retrieval must diversify into candidate instance terms. This applies to any future question asking for examples of a category; it does not apply to single-entity lookups or when evidence is explicitly labeled.
